The bundled org/conscrypt/conscrypt.properties declares BoringSSL revision
49f0329110a1d93a5febc2bceceedc655d995420. Its complete LICENSE was retrieved
from https://github.com/google/boringssl/blob/49f0329110a1d93a5febc2bceceedc655d995420/LICENSE
and is retained as BORINGSSL-LICENSE (OpenSSL/SSLeay/ISC notices).

Test-only dependency: org.conscrypt:conscrypt-openjdk-uber:2.5.2
Source: https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/conscrypt/conscrypt-openjdk-uber/2.5.2/conscrypt-openjdk-uber-2.5.2.jar
Archive SHA-256: eaf537d98e033d0f0451cd1b8cc74e02d7b55ec882da63c88060d806ba89c348
This artifact is not included in the APK. It declares the same BoringSSL revision.

Runtime native libraries were extracted from the official AAR, not the reference
APK: arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64. No hidden Android API bypass is used.

API19-21 exporter adapter (application code, dependency archive unchanged):
Conscrypt's KitKatPlatformOpenSSLSocketImplAdapter wraps its actual TLS socket,
but Conscrypt.exportKeyingMaterial accepts only the underlying Conscrypt type.
TlsSupport unwraps only this exact bundled adapter's private final `delegate`
field, then invokes the same public exporter on the same negotiated channel.
A changed layout fails closed. This is reflection on the pinned app-owned
library, not an Android hidden-API exemption or a trust/handshake bypass.
Source: https://github.com/google/conscrypt/blob/fd209de6167201e4f3bca5b99c6db9f08d1843c6/android/src/main/java/org/conscrypt/KitKatPlatformOpenSSLSocketImplAdapter.java
